name: DFRobot Gravity Heart Rate Monitor Sensor
description: DFRobot's Gravity optical heart-rate sensor (photoplethysmography): a SON1303 reflective sensor (green LED + photodetector) on the fingertip picks up the blood-volume pulse and a SON3130 rail-to-rail quad op-amp amplifies it. An onboard slide switch selects the output on the Signal pin: A = analog pulse waveform (0 to VCC), D = digital square pulse per beat (0 / VCC, comparator with hysteresis). Runs on 3.3-5.5 V (DFRobot rates the board 3.3-6 V, 5 V recommended; the SON3130 op-amp's recommended maximum is 5.5 V), under 10 mA. The output swings to VCC, so power it from 3.3 V for a 3.3 V board. Not a medical device. Sold as: DFRobot Gravity: Heart Rate Monitor Sensor for Arduino, SKU SEN0203, 28 x 24 mm round board with a PH2.0-3P Gravity connector (1 GND, 2 VCC, 3 Signal), finger strap included.
eli5: Strap it to your fingertip and its little green light watches your blood pulse, turning every heartbeat into a wiggle (or a click) your board can count.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground, pin 1 of the PH2.0-3P Gravity connector (black wire).

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, pin 2 (red wire), 3.3-5.5 V, under 10 mA. Use 3.3 V on a 3.3 V board: the Signal swings up to VCC.

pins.name: Signal
pins.description: Pin 3 (green/blue wire). Switch on A: analog pulse waveform 0..VCC (connect to an ADC pin). Switch on D: digital pulse, high (VCC) during each beat.

supplierQuery: DFRobot SEN0203 Gravity heart rate monitor sensor
buildNotes: Set the A/D slide switch to A for this analog wiring and code; with the switch on D the Signal is a 0/VCC square pulse (use SEN0203(pin, mode='digital')). A switch that doesn't match the code gives no reading.
Power it from 3.3 V on an ESP32 / Pico: the output (analog or digital) swings to VCC, so on 5 V it can exceed a 3.3 V pin.
The connector is a 2.0 mm PH2.0-3P Gravity socket: use the supplied Gravity cable (black GND, red VCC, green/blue Signal) or PH2.0-to-DuPont jumpers.
Keep the clear plastic film over the sensor (transparent tape replaces it); without it the module does not work.
Strap it to the fingertip pad with the band, not too tight, not too loose, and keep still; movement and bright light add noise.
On ESP32 use an ADC1 pin (ADC2 is unusable while Wi-Fi is on). Raspberry Pi has no ADC: use digital mode on a GPIO, or an ADS1115 / MCP3008.
Hobby/educational sensor, not a medical device.
